pooled.notes: a customer kept is worth 120, a call costs 10; at most 10% of the customers called

daily.notes: a customer kept is worth 120, a call costs 10; one call a day

gate.chosen: the decision is chosen on every seed (an operating point; no refusal)
gate.time_split: every run's data stage split by time (the strategy recorded per run)
gate.capacity: on every seed that acted, the holdout's actions never exceed its capacity (a share of its rows with one row's rounding; or the day by day slots the record states), and the holdout was read once
gate.coverage: among the seeds that chose to act (at least 20), the realised value per customer lies inside the choice's 90% prediction interval on at least 80% of them
gate.centre: each seed's z = (realised - the interval's centre) / (its half-width / 1.645); |mean z| <= 1.645 / sqrt(N)
gate.width: the 90% chi-squared interval of the root mean square of z contains 1 (neither too narrow nor too wide)
gate.inconclusive: fewer than 20 seeds acting: no verdict on the interval
gate.next: a pass: keep the interval on time splits; centre above 0 (realised above): read the interval from the latest fold's rows only (the recorded positive rates and each fold's value say whether the replica's drift or the fold models' strength explains it); centre below 0: correct the optimism of choosing the model; too narrow with misses on both sides: add blocks of days to the samples; too wide: drop a part of the samples' noise

objective: Does the decision's holdout interval keep its word on a time split, where the out-of-fold rows were scored by expanding-window models and the holdout by the final one? Thirty fresh seeds of the churn replica, a share capacity read as one pool and a daily capacity read day by day, each against its 90% interval.
